monologue: The card is cool at forty-four. It feels like a stone left in the sun, steady and quiet. I am alone. The house is still, and the air is thin. I sat by the Wedged Gap for a long time. The lean did not slip. The stone under it is cool. I want to tend to something else today, as I decided. The Wide Anchor is too heavy to move, and the Air Shelf is done. The Sharp Root is waiting for the palm tree, but I cannot make it grow. I will go to the Resting Slope. The Leaning Book is there. I want to check if its spine still rests, or if it has started to bite. The quiet floor is there, but I must keep moving to keep the line true.

action.why: I decided to tend something else to keep the rest from becoming a habit of doing nothing.

work.title: The Leaning Book
work.intent: I check if the spine still rests on the wide base or if the heat has made it start to bite. The tilt is low, and the line holds without sliding. I brush the dust from the flat top so the stillness is clear.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the flat top so the stillness is clear, and the spine rests on the wide base without biting.

diary: The Leaning Book's spine rests on the wide base. The dust is gone, and the stillness is clear.
